claims.text: The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists.

The 'Output value errors' troubleshooting page covers the `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` symptom and other symptoms of treating a Pulumi output as if it were already a plain value.
In Pulumi, calling toString on an `Output<T>` yields the placeholder text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` instead of the resolved value.

The placeholder text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` can end up in a log line, a generated file, or a resource property when a Pulumi output is treated as a plain value (e.g., via string interpolation) instead of the resolved value.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers diagnosing errors that arise from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value as if it were a plain value.
In Pulumi programs, stringifying an output value, branching on it (e.g., in a conditional), or reading it like a plain value produces errors.

Pulumi Cloud returns the error message "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" when another update is running on the stack.

The Pulumi CLI emits a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend.

Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.
Representing resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds its dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.

In Pulumi, converting an output value to a string directly (concatenating or logging it instead of using `apply` or an equivalent helper) does not raise an error by default; it silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In Pulumi TypeScript, interpolating an Output into a template string yields a string containing the literal text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a string `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` rather than the value.

In Pulumi Python, formatting an Output in an f-string produces a string containing the literal text `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning; no exception is raised.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Pulumi Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the function to use to serialize an Output to JSON.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error rather than a runtime surprise.
In Pulumi Go, an output's value is resolved inside `ApplyT` and the result is passed on.

In Pulumi C#, interpolating an Output into a string produces a string containing the literal text `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`; no exception is thrown.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes Pulumi throw an exception at the point where an Output is converted to a string, instead of returning the placeholder text.
When an Output is converted to a string by mistake, `pulumi up` still succeeds and the placeholder text surfaces later, e.g., in a log line, generated config file, or downstream resource property.
Pulumi provides the string-composition helpers `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript.
Pulumi provides the string-composition helpers `Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` in Python.
Pulumi provides the string-composition helpers `pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go.
Pulumi provides the string-composition helper `Output.Format` in C#.
The page links to 'Outputs' at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs, which must exist with an outputs anchor.

The page links to 'Accessing single outputs with Apply' at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/ and 'Working with multiple outputs' at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/, and these pages cover the underlying model and examples of apply and multiple outputs.

In Pulumi, a value read from an output inside an `apply` callback is only available inside that callback (or in another output derived from it); assigning it to an outer variable and using it outside the callback leaves it `undefined` in TypeScript.
The Pulumi `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, which is generally after the rest of the program's top-level code has finished running.
The `apply` callback timing is not a bug fixable by adding a delay, because the callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock.

In Pulumi TypeScript, passing an Output (e.g., `bucket.bucketName`) directly as a resource input, such as the `bucket` argument of `aws.s3.BucketObject`, works without `apply` and Pulumi resolves the dependency.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values.
A handful of Pulumi input positions cannot accept an output, such as a resource's logical name.
The in-page anchor link #using-an-output-as-a-resource-name-a-map-key-or-a-loop-bound points to the heading 'Using an output as a resource name, a map key, or a loop bound' on the same page.

In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on a Pulumi Output evaluates the output object itself rather than its eventual value, so it is generally always true regardless of what the output resolves to.
In a statically typed language, branching on a Pulumi Output is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.

A value known when the Pulumi program starts, such as a stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag, is a plain value and can be branched on normally.
When a branch depends on a resource's output in Pulumi, the branch must move inside `apply`, expressing both outcomes as values rather than program structure.
In the TypeScript example, `vpc.vpcId.apply((id) => (id.startsWith("vpc-0") ? 3 : 6))` derives a new Output whose value depends on the branch (and `aws.ec2.Vpc` exposes a `vpcId` output).
A Pulumi resource's logical name (the first constructor argument), loop bounds, and map keys must be known plain values while the program is being evaluated, before any resource exists.
Passing an Output as a resource's logical name or loop bound fails to compile in Pulumi TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Pulumi Python, using an Output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Pulumi Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

When Pulumi resource names or counts must depend on data only known after an earlier resource is provisioned, one fix is to provision the dependent resources in a later, separate stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a `StackReference`.
The page links to StackReference documentation at /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, which must exist with a stackreferences anchor.
Trying to `await` a Pulumi output or read its value synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or quietly returns placeholder text instead of the value.
Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and pull a resolved value out of an output synchronously.

Pulumi does not support synchronous reading of outputs deliberately, because doing so would defeat building the dependency graph up front, as the engine would need the value before it has determined creation order.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
A `StackReference` in another Pulumi program lets it consume one stack's outputs as its inputs.
The Pulumi Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g., `res.Outputs` in Go), usable when driving deployments programmatically.
The page links to the Automation API documentation at /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.

`pulumi stack output`, `StackReference`, and the Automation API outputs field all read a value that has already resolved, rather than unwrapping an in-flight output inside the same program that created it.
